```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
```

## Load the weather data 

```{r}
library(p8105.datasets)
data("weather_df")
```

## Remember this plot..? 

```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) + 
  geom_point(aes(color = name), alpha = .5)
```

## Labels

```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) + 
  geom_point(aes(color = name), alpha = .5) +
  labs(
    title = "Temperature plot",
    x = "Minimum daily temperature (C)",
    y = "Maximum daily temperature (C)", 
    color = "Location",
    caption = "Data from the rnoaa package; temperatures in 2017."
  )
```


## Scales

Start with the same plot; x and y scales

X axis scale
```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) + 
  geom_point(aes(color = name), alpha = .5) +
  labs(
    title = "Temperature plot",
    x = "Minimum daily temperature (C)",
    y = "Maximum daily temperature (C)", 
    color = "Location",
    caption = "Data from the rnoaa package; temperatures in 2017."
  ) + 
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(-15, 0, 15),
    labels = c("-15 ºC", "0", "15")
  )
```

Adding y axis scale

```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) + 
  geom_point(aes(color = name), alpha = .5) +
  labs(
    title = "Temperature plot",
    x = "Minimum daily temperature (C)",
    y = "Maximum daily temperature (C)", 
    color = "Location",
    caption = "Data from the rnoaa package; temperatures in 2017."
  ) + 
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(-15, 0, 15),
    labels = c("-15 ºC", "0", "15"), 
    limits = c(-20, 30)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    trans = "sqrt", 
    position = "right"
  )
```


Look at colour scales 

```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) + 
  geom_point(aes(color = name), alpha = .5) +
  labs(
    title = "Temperature plot",
    x = "Minimum daily temperature (C)",
    y = "Maximum daily temperature (C)", 
    caption = "Data from the rnoaa package; temperatures in 2017."
  ) +
  scale_color_hue(
    name = "Location",  
    h = c(100, 300))
```

Viridis package: 

```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) + 
  geom_point(aes(color = name), alpha = .5) +
  labs(
    title = "Temperature plot",
    x = "Minimum daily temperature (C)",
    y = "Maximum daily temperature (C)", 
    caption = "Data from the rnoaa package; temperatures in 2017."
  ) +
 viridis:: scale_color_viridis(
   name = "Location",
   discrete = TRUE)
```


## Themes

Themes are used to modify non-data elements of a plot (ie. controls things like background color and location of the the legend)

Shift the legend 

```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) + 
  geom_point(aes(color = name), alpha = .5) +
  labs(
    title = "Temperature plot",
    x = "Minimum daily temperature (C)",
    y = "Maximum daily temperature (C)", 
    caption = "Data from the rnoaa package; temperatures in 2017."
  ) +
 viridis:: scale_color_viridis(
   name = "Location",
   discrete = TRUE) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Change the overall theme 

```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) + 
  geom_point(aes(color = name), alpha = .5) +
  labs(
    title = "Temperature plot",
    x = "Minimum daily temperature (C)",
    y = "Maximum daily temperature (C)", 
    caption = "Data from the rnoaa package; temperatures in 2017."
  ) +
 viridis:: scale_color_viridis(
   name = "Location",
   discrete = TRUE) +
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```
